**Русский:** [RELEASE_NOTES-r31a.ru.md](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/r31a/docs/RELEASE_NOTES-r31a.ru.md) · **Español:** [RELEASE_NOTES-r31a.es.md](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/r31a/docs/RELEASE_NOTES-r31a.es.md)

For **Akai MPC Sample stock firmware 1.3.0.12**. Continues r30d-beta4; installed firmware is never rewritten. **Arrange is a beta feature**: back up your projects before arranging them.

![Arrange](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/r31a/docs/media/r31a/arrange-en.png)

## Arrange (beta)

A song timeline inside the Song screen: **Song → Shift+B1** (transport stopped). Full instructions: [Arrange guide](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/r31a/docs/ARRANGE_GUIDE.md).

- **Rows are free lanes** that play together. A **Seq block** is a live window into a stock sequence (re-record the sequence and the block follows); a **pattern** is your own copy for variations and does not change with its source.
- **Add a sequence by tapping its pad** and confirming; **B3 New** on an empty place lists the sequences with notes plus *Empty pattern*.
- **Select** with a DATA click, or hold DATA and draw a rectangle across rows. **Hold Note Repeat + DATA / fader** moves a block or the whole selection, drawn at its new place; release applies. **Erase** deletes, **Shift+Erase** copies right after, **Chop** cuts, **Shift − / +** undo / redo.
- **Grouped Actions menu** (Shift+B3): Add / Block / Track / Song, including *Track: delete* (with confirmation), *Block: rename pattern* and *Track: rename*.
- **Play / Stop** through the stock Song transport, **Shift+Play from the cursor**, playback stops at the end of the last block. **Loop** (lit when on) loops the range, the selection, the block or the whole song, rounded to bars.
- **Edits while playing are heard**: moving, copying or deleting blocks and editing a Seq block re-render the song without stopping.
- **Block colours** follow the sequence colour, names are centred. The **grid follows bar lines** (beats when zoomed in) and scrolls and zooms with the blocks; the cursor reads bar.beat. **Stop + DATA** jumps to the start / end.
- **Export the arrangement**: Shift+B1 opens the stock Song Export menu (mixdown and stems) for the whole arrangement; your Song steps are restored afterwards.

## Piano Roll inside a block

- Opens on top of Arrange (B3 Open, Shift+DATA click or *Block: open in Piano Roll*); B1 returns.
- Header shows the block's place in the song; the ruler counts **song bars**; a **playhead** runs inside the block and **Shift+B2 Follow** keeps it in view.
- Each row shows its pad and the **beginning of the sample name**.
- **Shift+pads** select whole rows. **Shift+Erase** copies the selection or, with nothing selected, pastes at the cursor; the clipboard survives opening another block, so you can copy from a sequence into a pattern. **Erase** deletes on release.
- Pads choose a row; click or B3 inserts an event in an empty cell. **Hold Note Repeat + DATA / fader** moves the selected events.
- **Seq blocks are edited in place** with the stock Undo / Redo (Shift − / +).

## Renaming with the Mod text input

Patterns and Arrange tracks are renamed like files in the browser: pads type letters (multi-tap, Shift for capitals) and light with their letters, DATA moves the cursor, **K1** switches between pad and encoder input and is highlighted on screen, B3 saves.

## Mixer

![Mixer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/r31a/docs/media/r31a/mixer-en.png)

## Other changes since r30d-beta4

- **Logs in their own folder.** The mod's journals (`MPC_CLONE_TRIAL.txt`, `MPC_MOD_EVENTS.txt`, `MPC_MOD_CONSOLE.txt`, `MPC_MOD_ENTRY.txt`) are now written to **`Logs/`** inside the mod folder (`autorun/Logs/`, `autorun/mods/AM-Mod/Logs/` or `autorun/os/AM-Mod/Logs/`). The first start removes the old copies beside the mod files (known names only). **Installer 1.6.0** collects the logs from both places for bug reports.
- **Power button:** the shutdown dialog has **B1 Cancel, B2 Bootloader, B3 Power off**. B2 and B3 first save a copy of the project to `Projects/Mod-Exit-Last.xpj`; if that save fails the mod stays on.
- **Rear input routing:** independent Rear L / Rear R monitor, pan and level (Input settings → Rear → B2 Routing, and rows in Mixer → Input → ROUTE). Rear monitoring goes through the stock path and reaches the Mixer Master. Sample Record no longer has Shift+B2 Routing; B2 is still To Seq.
- **To Seq:** the recorded take starts at the exact position, several waiting notes are kept, and nothing is placed before Play.
- **Sequential Song repeats** play as set; the playback list follows Repeats changes and Undo.
- **SD Card Access under SampleBoot** releases and restores the `autorun/mods/<name>` binding correctly; D.S.B and a plain card keep working.
- **Sample Swap / browser replacement** keeps its target pad pinned; **Screen Mirror** streams more frames.
- **Piano Roll** shows which sequence is edited and the cursor position.
- **Boot screen and About** show **r31a**.

## Experimental

- **Synth Keys recording:** Mixer → Synth → 16 Levels → **Shift+Seq Record** turns on a session-only trial that records the synth keys into the sequence (it needs an empty pad A16) and plays them back through the synth. Not yet checked by a user on a physical MPC.

## Status

The Arrange features above were tested on a physical MPC in the Arrange test builds up to Test 25, which use the same code. **Not yet checked on a device:** the final r31a package itself, the move of the logs to `Logs/` (it changes the start scripts) and the Synth Keys recording trial.

## Limits

- **No Mixer while Song or Arrange plays**: the stock Song screen refuses to be re-entered during playback, so Knob FX shows *Stop playback to open the Mixer*.
- No recording in Arrange (Rec, audio takes) and no named song sections yet; very long songs (more than 128 bars) are not supported yet.
- Seq 128 is Arrange's service slot; after Arrange the current sequence may be Seq 128.
- A block cannot be opened while the song plays.
- Stock firmware and older Am MOD versions may drop the Arrange data when they re-save a project.

[Arrange guide](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/r31a/docs/ARRANGE_GUIDE.md) · [Known limitations](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/r31a/docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) · [Installation](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/r31a/docs/INSTALL.md) · [Changelog](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/r31a/CHANGELOG.md)

## Downloads

- `am-mod-r31a.zip` — the mod package (SHA-256 in `SHA256SUMS.txt`).
- `MPC-Sample-Mod-Installer.exe` — installer 1.6.0 for Windows (recommended; installs to the SD card or USB drive and collects the logs from `Logs/`).

releases.body:
# Am MOD r30d beta4 — synth, Input ROUTE, bootloader exit

> **BETA — r30d-beta4.** Compatibility with other mods and boot menus (Stock, SampQOL, D.S.B, SampleBoot, mpc-boot-thingy) is still being tested. Back up your projects and card first. Items marked *pending* passed host/emulator checks but still need a check on a physical MPC.

For **Akai MPC Sample stock firmware 1.3.0.12**. This release continues r30c-beta1; installed firmware is never rewritten.

![Synth modules](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/raw/main/docs/media/r30d/synth-modules-en.png)

## Fixes in beta4

- **Tidy card root:** the power report and the status markers now live in one folder, `AmMod/` (`AmMod/MPC_POWER_AUDIT.txt`, `AmMod/Status/`), instead of `MPC_POWER_AUDIT.txt` and `MPC_TRIAL_STATUS/` at the card root, so several systems can share a card. The first start removes the old report and the old marker names; your own files are never touched. (Suggested by the SampleBoot author.)
- **SampleBoot 1.0.3 or later** no longer shows card-root settings files such as `mpcqol.conf` inside the mod's folder, so no `ROOT_FILES=""` change is needed; it remains the workaround for older SampleBoot versions.
- **Installer 1.5.1:** the SampleBoot message is now a hint for older versions only. Bug-report logs are also collected from the boot-menu folders and SampleBoot's `last-boot.log`.

## Fixes in beta3

- **SampleBoot:** Am MOD installs to `autorun/mods/AM-Mod/` and starts from the SampleBoot menu. **Exit to bootloader** (Mod Settings → About) now returns to the **SampleBoot menu**, as it does for D.S.B. Checked on a physical MPC.
- **Boot menu art:** the Am MOD logo appears in the SampleBoot carousel (`sampleboot.png`) and on the D.S.B record (`dsb-record.png`); SampleBoot shows the name “Am MOD”.
- **Installer 1.5.1** detects SampleBoot and installs into the right folder. If SampleBoot's `ROOT_FILES` setting shows a card-root file such as `mpcqol.conf` inside `mods/`, Am MOD refuses to start (its sandbox check rejects a writable file from the card); the installer warns, and the fix is `ROOT_FILES=""` in `autorun/sampleboot/sampleboot.conf` (SampQOL then does not see its card-root settings).

## Fixes in beta2

- **USB inputs** (USB, USB L, USB R) now go through the Input track: Input FX, fader, pan and mute apply to them. USB was mislabelled as a different input before, and its signal arrives on a native channel pair the mod did not process.
- **Input list order:** Source, Mode, Monitor, Threshold, Record via, Record track, Record FX, Tuner, MIDI In. **Monitor** has Off / Auto / On for every source and enables Rear monitoring from the Mixer. Record track shows "-" for Master and Input.
- **Pan on K1 of the FX chain** for tracks, the Input track and Master (Pad Bank + K1 resets it to centre). On the Input ROUTE tab K1 = Pan, K2 = Threshold, K3 = Source for every source, Rear included; the L/R pan and level of the Rear channels stay in Rear Routing.
- **Rear mode:** the Mode row for Rear starts in **Stereo** (listed first, the default when you choose Rear) and offers Rear L, Rear R, L+R Split and L+R Mix. The monitor follows the mode: Rear L plays the left jack only, Rear R the right one, the others both. The MPC's physical output-level panel shows the Rear signal.
- D.S.B: the record label under AM Mod now shows the current version.

## Synth (Mixer pad 13)

- **Five modules, nine pages.** Tone (Oscillators, Mixer), Envelope (Amp, Filter envelope), Keys, Filter + LFO, Voices (Voices, Controller). Modules sit on pads 13–16 and 9; **hold Loop and press a pad**, or step with **+ / −**. The **DATA** encoder flips the pages inside a module.
- **More sound.** Second oscillator (wave, mix, semitone, fine), sub oscillator, noise, drive, a separate filter envelope with amount, key tracking, four LFO shapes, bend range, unison with detune and spread, glide, velocity sensitivity.
- **One row of knobs.** K1–K3 hold the frequently used parameter; the rarely used one is on **Shift+K** and is shown above the knob while Shift is held. See the [synth guide](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/SYNTH_GUIDE.md) for every page.
- **Keys page = Tune tab.** K1 Transpose16 / Shift Layout, K2 Tonic / Shift Role, K3 Scale / Shift Colour; values read like the Tune tab, e.g. “D# (P)”, “Natural Minor (P)”, “−4 st”.
- **Fader** (Off / Mod / Pitch) is K1 of the Controller page. Parameters such as LFO Depth, Sub, Noise, Drive and Key track read “Off” at zero.
- **Takeover.** The synth's K knobs follow the Parameter takeover mode (Pickup, Scaled, Jump) like the rest of the Mixer.
- Entering the synth in the Mixer clears the track selection; pads 9–12 show the Input track's effects, because the synth is the Input track's source. Pad 14 no longer leaves the synth.
- Thumbnails mirror the pad layout; the big module drawing on the left shows the live waveform, envelope or filter curve.

## Input and recording

- **Shift+Sample opens the Input ROUTE list from every screen** (Seq, Step Edit, compressor, Project), never the stock Input Config. Rows: Source (Mic / Rear / USB / Resample / Synth), Mode (Rear and USB: Stereo, L, R …), Monitor, Threshold, Tuner and record rows. K1 Pan, K2 Threshold, K3 Source; **B2 FX, B3 MIDI In**, Shift+B2 opens the stock screen. The list scrolls and the pad layout stays as you left it.
- **Sample Record:** K1 selects the input Source (including Synth), Shift+K1 the Rear/USB mode. With the **16 Levels** synth keyboard on, the knobs follow the Tune tab (K1 Transpose16 / Layout, K2 Tonic / Role, K3 Scale / Colour) and redraw when Shift is released.
- The synth always follows the master volume; the old *Direct out* and *Mic layer* options are gone. Changing the Input source takes the Input off the synth.

## Piano Roll

- **Area selection:** hold **DATA**, turn the encoder (time) and move the fader (rows); the covered area is selected live. Release DATA to keep it. A short DATA click without movement still selects the note under the cursor (Shift adds).

## Layout swap

- **Layout and Transpose16 swapped** on the Tune tab, the synth Keys page and Sample Record: **K1 = Transpose16, Shift+K1 = Layout**. Resetting the knob follows the new order.

## MIDI

- Global MIDI/synth defaults, a **MIDI Buttons** page (scrolling list, B3 assign, B2 delete/cancel, faders assignable) and a fader MIDI source.
- Controller modifier buttons (for example Shift on a MiniLab) act as plain buttons unless the MPC's own Shift is held, so a keyboard Shift no longer holds the MPC Shift.
- MIDI In from Input Config: B3 / Shift+B2 switch the input mode, Shift+B3 Buttons, Shift+B2 Clear; the MIDI synth list scrolls.

## Effects

- **Henry Skillz** effects HS Saturator, HS Bass Focus and HS Heat (DSP from [hs-mpc-plugins](https://github.com/Holla-Back-Entertainment/hs-mpc-plugins), used with permission), with their own visuals, a page tab strip and a Heat page highlight. Add Effect has an HS author tab and name search (B2). *Pending device check.*

## Bootloader and D.S.B

- **Mod Settings → About → Exit to bootloader** (B3 confirms, B1 cancels) saves a project copy to `Projects/Mod-Exit-Last` and returns to the **D.S.B menu**; without D.S.B the MPC starts stock firmware. See [Boot menus and bootloader exit](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/BOOTLOADERS.md).
- **D.S.B state carry-over:** D.S.B's “start OK” marking now reaches the card's real state file, so a healthy Am MOD start is no longer counted as a crash and the menu stops offering Stock after two starts.
- The D.S.B boot journal and the state-fix log are copied beside the mod on the card for diagnostics (`dsb-boot.log`, `dsb-state-fix.log`).
- Fast-boot idea: pick **AM Mod** once in a boot menu and use **Exit to bootloader** whenever you want a different system.

## Other

- Browser search shows a **Find** label; Shift+B2 clears the whole text.
- Synth Hold note holds the last 16 Levels note and shows it highlighted.
- Synth FX tail hold and fade-out remove clicks when notes end.

## Limits

- The synth modules, Input ROUTE, takeover for synth knobs, Piano Roll area selection and the layout swap were finished after the last full device check: *pending* hardware verification.
- To Seq recording of a Mic take may not play the new sample in the sequence in every situation; logs from the device are welcome.
- Exit to bootloader hands over to **D.S.B** only. SampleBoot and mpc-boot-thingy are supported for starting the mod; returning to them from the mod is not implemented.
- Cross-mod Load/Save of Internal projects (Am MOD, Stock, SampQOL) is not fully certified.

See [Known limitations](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md), [Installation](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) and the [changelog](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

releases.name: FW 1.4 plug-and-play card (pre-release)
releases.body:
Plug-and-play card for the **MPC Sample, firmware 1.4.0.7 only**: D.S.B, HS 25, HS Treble Bass and 16 HS effects (official plugins).

Unzip to the root of the SD card and follow `README-INSTALL.txt`. Back up your card first. Taking the card out returns the Sample to stock.

**Pre-release:** the Developer Mode and Enhancements menu steps are taken from Akai's SDK docs and have not been confirmed on a real Sample. The launcher only runs on the exact 1.4.0.7 firmware.

No SampQOL (it doesn't work on 1.4). Other providers' OS can't be added to this card; use a separate card per OS.

Licences: includes third-party parts under GPL-3, AGPL-3 and the JUCE licence; texts are in `DSB-Performance/os/dsb-os/licenses`. To request the corresponding source for the GPL/AGPL parts, open an issue on this repository.

Unofficial. Not made, endorsed or supported by Akai Professional or inMusic.

releases.name: FW 1.3 tester build (pre-release)

Early tester build of the plug-and-play card for the **MPC Sample, firmware 1.3.0.12 only**: boot menu, D.S.B, HS 25, HS FX (Para EQ, Tube Strip, Saturator), SampQOL 0.4.0 and a Stock entry.

**Not the latest of everything, and not fully tested.** D.S.B and HS 25 are rebuilt from source and have not run on a real Sample yet. Stems and project import are untested. The HS QOL add-ons and HS 20, 30, 40 and 60 are not in this build.

Back up your SD card first. Unzip, copy `autorun` and `HS-OS` to the top level of the card, power on and follow `README-TESTERS.txt`. Pull the card and the Sample is stock again. `ADD-OTHER-OS.md` covers adding another OS to the menu.

SampQOL OS is by Snare Bes, included with the author's approval; see its licence in `autorun/os/SampQOL-0.4.0/LICENSE.txt`. Boot menu follows SampleBoot by Alessandro D'Esposito (MIT). Other third-party parts are under the GPL-3; licence texts are in `LICENSES/`. To request the corresponding source for the GPL parts, open an issue on this repository.

Unofficial. Not made, endorsed or supported by Akai Professional, inMusic or the SampQOL author.

releases.name: LA Version 2.0I
releases.body:
## LA Version 2.0I

- **Phantom pads, buttons and wheel fixed.** At power-on the stock app can switch the panel's MIDI port to timestamp framing (every message wrapped in a 32-byte block with the time). Linux keeps that setting for whoever opens the port next. On those boots the MPC 600 S read the timestamps as messages: pads you didn't touch played, pages opened by themselves (Input Effects), the wheel jumped. Whether it happened depended on how far the stock app got before being stopped, so it came and went between boots. The MPC 600 S now switches framing off on the panel, the MIDI jacks and USB MIDI when it opens them. `mpc-os.log` on the card records `panel port: plain bytes (framing off)` at each start.
- **Real presses no longer thrown away.** A raw recording of the panel showed that pad hits don't move the wheel or press buttons, and that turning the wheel doesn't play pads. The filters that assumed they did are gone. They were dropping pad hits under velocity 80 for 0.4 s after the wheel moved (ghost notes), single wheel steps just after a pad, B1-B3 and -/+ just after a pad, and a softer pad played together with a harder neighbour. Pad Thresh (default 30) is the pads' one filter for light hits. The guards after K1-K3 and the slider stay.
- **Track Mute setting** (Additional Settings 2): **AT ONCE** (default, as since 2.0F) or **NEXT NOTE** (as before 2.0F: a mute lets the sound end, an unmute waits for the track's next note).
- **Clear Pgm asks which program.** SHIFT + B3 on Program Config starts on the program shown, and the wheel picks any other program with sounds. Before, reaching another program meant moving the track onto it, and Undo after clearing could leave the track on another program, so a chopped sequence played another program's pads (chops "out of order").
- **Start screen:** Original MPC design by Roger Linn, Akai Electric Co., Ltd.
- Manual updated.

releases.name: LA Version 2.0H
releases.body:
## LA Version 2.0H

- **Knobs no longer move things by themselves.** A knob (or the slider, or the main volume) resting between two positions sends a constant flicker, and each reading was taken as a turn. Zoomed in on Trim, a resting Zone End knob could nudge Zone End and make the view jump from Start to End; on Trim, K3 could move the cursor to Do. Now a control has to move two steps from rest before it counts. Turning still takes every step, turning back takes two, and after 0.4 s still it is at rest again. A flicker never changes anything. Also: B1-B3, -/+ and the wheel's push just after a knob turn are ignored as the panel shaking (as after a pad press), and a flickering knob no longer makes light pad presses get ignored.
- **Playhead.** While a pad plays, a solid line moves along the waveform where the sound is, on Trim, Loop and Zone Assign, to set Zone End by eye.
- **MPC60 pitching.** Every sound now plays at another pitch by zero-order hold, taken from the MPC60: each output is the stored sample at or before the play position, never blended, with the pitch step in 4.12 fixed point as on the MPC60 and MPC3000 chips. Pitched down it has the stepped, metallic edge, pitched up the crunch. Pitch on Sample New Sound (before a sound is stored) stays high quality. The manual has a new chapter, **Pitching**, comparing the MPC60, the MPC3000's 8-point interpolation, modern methods and the stock OS, with measurements.
- **USB Indiv Out knobs.** K1 picks the track (or pad), K2 sets its Indiv Out Volume, K3 its Output.

Everything from 2.0A to 2.0G is included.

releases.name: LA Version 2.0G
releases.body:
## LA Version 2.0G

- **USB Indiv Out is eight outputs.** The Layout setting is gone: all eight USB channels are outputs, each a mono channel (1-8) or a stereo pair (1-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8). The main mix no longer goes over USB alongside them, so a pad or track on an output is not sent to the computer twice. For the whole song in stereo, use USB Audio Out with USB Indiv Out off.
- **In mix is gone.** The MPC's own line out and headphones always play every track, whether or not it is on an output.

Everything from 2.0A to 2.0F is included.

releases.body:
## For MPC Sample firmware 1.3 only

This page contains **GRIDZILLA 1.2.9 for firmware 1.3**. Download **GRIDZILLA.zip** from the assets below.

Using firmware 1.4? Open the separate **[GRIDZILLA-1.4 repository](https://github.com/ZootedandRebooted/GRIDZILLA-1.4)**.

## GRIDZILLA 1.2.9 — Stability Update

GRIDZILLA adds instruments, MIDI editing, song arrangement, mixing and FX automation to the MPC Sample. It runs from the SD card without flashing Akai firmware.

This update adds a clean Master for new songs and brings the Henry Skillz FX collection, selected-pad Melodic editing, sequence looping in Grid and Melodic, a synchronized Loop light, and safer Mixer editing during project loading. The current release passed its hardware qualification, audio checks and normal reboot test on the MPC Sample.

### Updated Mixer and FX

Open the Mixer with **SHIFT + Pad 5**. Select a pad or **MASTER**, open **Inserts**, and choose an empty slot.

**Nine Henry Skillz effects are included:**

- Heat
- Pump
- Bus Compressor
- Channel Strip
- Para EQ
- Tube Strip
- Bass Focus
- Crush
- Saturator

Henry's effects are available on pad and Master inserts. **Flex Beat** is available on pad insert slots; Master inserts use the nine Henry effects. Open an occupied slot to edit it, and use **Next Page** for additional controls while playback continues.

**New empty songs now start with four clear Master insert slots.** Native PAD FX stays available independently of those user slots. Empty slots stay empty after save/reload, and effects already saved in existing projects are preserved. The Flex editor also clears stale Master-effect references during project changes.

The Mixer provides four insert slots, colored meters, pad and Master faders, and SHIFT controls for mute and solo. Faders range from silence to +12 dB, with 0 dB at unity. Existing saved levels are retained.

Henry Skillz's DSP is credited in the included **HENRY-FX-NOTICE.txt**, with its MIT license.

### Loop the sequence you are editing

- Open Grid with **SHIFT + SEQ**, then press **LOOP** to enable or disable looping for that sequence.
- The same control works in **Melodic** mode.
- With Loop enabled, **STOP → PLAY** restarts the sequence you are editing at its loop start.
- **SHIFT + PLAY** retains the native resume behavior, and saved sequence loop boundaries are preserved.
- The **Loop button lights up when looping is enabled** and stays synchronized across modes, including Grid, Melodic, Song, Mixer and Sample.
- The Arranger keeps its own song/cycle loop range.

### Melodic editing and transpose

Melodic mode now shows **only the selected pad's notes**, including their per-note tuning. The pad label identifies what you are editing. Switching pads changes the displayed notes; an empty pad shows an empty view.

Chord selection and transposition apply only to that pad, even when other pads have notes at the same pitch or time. Return to **Grid** to see the complete pattern. Single-note and chord transpose, copy, Undo/Redo, and native save/reload were checked on hardware.

### Instruments, arrangement and automation

- **16 LEVELS** opens the instrument library and chord mode. Play single notes or one-pad chords from triads through 13ths.
- Edit recorded notes in Melodic and change an existing instrument while the Song plays.
- **SNAP** aligns newly recorded note starts to the selected grid; **SNAP OFF** preserves performed timing. Existing notes stay in place.
- Use Grid and Melodic Tools, **ADD SEQUENCE**, and sequence-position controls to build and edit your arrangement.
- Use **TOUCH, LATCH or WRITE** to record FX changes and **READ** to play them back. Flex Beat supports MIX automation and individual ON/OFF points on the grid.
- The stopped-state “STOP” text has been removed from the Arranger bar.

### Stability and hardware verification

Mixer insert, removal, Undo and Redo actions are temporarily unavailable while a project loads, then return when loading finishes. This addresses the identified Mixer load-readiness issue.

Release qualification covers:

- Grid and Melodic Loop on/off, repeated loop playback, Stop/Play restart and cross-mode Loop-light checks.
- Song-to-Grid handoff, repeated sequence occurrences, saved loop bounds and eight reload cycles.
- Selected-pad display, pad switching, chord and single-note transpose, copy, Undo/Redo, and save/reload checks.
- Audio timing and pitch checks.
- Empty Master creation and save/reload, native PAD FX state and playback, and exact preservation of saved Master effects.
- Flex Beat controls, bypass, audio playback, save/reload, removal and Undo/Redo, including use alongside custom Master inserts.
- Ten Henry FX editor cycles, including all 41 Para EQ pages during playback, plus removal and Undo/Redo.
- Normal startup and reboot, with the test device's existing project and musical events preserved.

The Loop, Melodic, controls and Arranger modules retain their previously qualified binaries. The new Master and Mixer changes passed the additional checks above.

**No captured faults occurred in the successful release qualification runs.** Qualification covered the workflows listed above on the tested MPC Sample.

### Firmware 1.3 download and installation

Download **[GRIDZILLA.zip](https://github.com/ZootedandRebooted/GRIDZILLA/releases/download/GRIDZILLA/GRIDZILLA.zip)** below. This is the tested 1.2.9 Stability Update for an existing supported GRIDZILLA installation on firmware 1.3.

Save your project and back up your SD card before updating. Extract the complete package and follow **INSTALLATION GUIDE.txt** for installation and rollback. Keep `install.sh`, `autorun`, and `WaveGrid` together.

The illustrated **GRIDZILLA-User-Guide.pdf** and **GRIDZILLA-Video.mov** are separate release assets. Use the included installation guide for this update's current instructions.

The ZIP contains runtime files, installation scripts, documentation and license notices. **GRIDZILLA implementation source, development files, credentials and user projects are not included.**

MPCkit 0.5.6 is a beta. Keep a copy of any project you care about before opening it in MPCkit.

## What's new

- **Fill a bank by dropping files.** Drop several WAV files, or a folder, onto an empty bank: on its letter, or on any of its pads. The first 16 files, in name order, fill pads 1–16. Files that can't be used are skipped, and MPCkit tells you which.
- **Rename a pad's sample.** Edit the name in Pad settings and click **Rename**, or press Enter. Only the copy in the exported project gets the new name; your original file is never changed. Pads that share the file get the new name too.
- **Clear bank.** One button empties a whole bank of pads, or removes a whole bank of sequences. MPCkit asks first and lists what will go.
- **Play on click.** A switch on the Pads tab turns off the sound when you click a pad or change its tuning. The Play button always plays. The switch is on each time MPCkit starts.

The command-line tool, `mpckit-cli`, gains `-fill`, `-rename`, `-clearbank`, `-rmseqbank` and `-trim`. `-trim` sets where a pad's sample starts and ends. The window's start and end editor is coming in 0.6.0.

releases.body:
Tape Workshop v211 fixes the crash reported in #3 when pressing Plus or Minus on the plug-in preset page.

The preset page had no Minus/Plus callback, while the host called that callback unconditionally. Minus and Plus now use the same bounded preset navigation as the Data wheel. The host also checks for an absent handler before calling it. Built-in presets, folders, filtered lists, empty lists and list boundaries are covered by regression checks.

## Download and install

- **Tape-Workshop-v211-Signed-Update.zip** — signed OS update for an existing Tape Workshop installation. Upload it in the browser updater, save your project, then confirm INSTALL physically on the MPC. For an existing SD installation, the ZIP contains the autorun folder; preserve your existing root launcher, Melodee folder, projects, samples and plug-ins. This is not a fresh-install package with the entire plug-in library.
- **Melodee-v211-source.tar.gz** — matching source, including the host fix and regression tests; not needed on the SD card.
- **Tape-Workshop-v211-SHA256SUMS.txt** — download checksums.

The fix is in the OS. Replacing Sub Foundry or obtaining a version-matched plug-in pack is not required for this specific null-callback fault. Existing plug-in folders are not replaced by the signed updater.

This release includes the current community build through v210, including the opt-in Key Sync setting. Automatic BPM/key labeling of newly recorded takes remains removed. Orbit is a separate plug-in and is not installed by this update.

## Validation

ARM64 build, full native model regression suite, preset navigation regressions, layout checks and signed-package verification passed. On-device confirmation of the reported crash fix is still pending; the input-distortion investigation is not claimed fixed by this release.

releases.body:
## New track, bank and pad mixer

Mix all 16 tracks, individual pads across banks A–H, and the master from the new dark mixer interface. Includes real audio meters, volume and pan, mute/solo, and quick FX access.

### Open the mixer

Press **Pad FX + Knob FX together**, or **hold Data → GO → MIXER**.

- Turn **Data** to select a track; press to open its bank mixer.
- Select a pad and press **Data** for Pad Details.
- **B1** Back · **B2** Mute/Solo · **B3** FX.
- Strip pages: **K1** channel · **K2** volume · **K3** pan.
- Pad Details: **K1** volume · **K2** pan · **K3** Send A.
- Tap **Pad Bank** to cycle A–H; Shift + tap goes backward.
- Select the master strip and press Data for master level, balance and mono/stereo.
- Save your project to retain mixer settings.

Pad chains support built-in effects. Track, bus and master chains also support installed compatible effect plug-ins.

### Download and install

The single download contains **only `autorun/`**. It updates the OS; plug-ins are unchanged and are not included.

Use the signed ZIP in the Tape Workshop browser updater. Save your project, upload the ZIP, then confirm **B3 / INSTALL physically on the MPC** and let it restart.

For an SD-card copy, extract the ZIP and copy its `autorun` folder to the card root, merging/replacing the existing folder after making a backup. Keep your existing root `autorun.sh`, `Melodee` folder and plug-ins. Firmware 1.4 requires Developer Mode and the existing root launcher.

The MPC ARM build, native navigation/regression tests, core audio/save-load tests, signature verification and source layout checks passed. Installed and the track mixer screen verified on an MPC Sample.

[Corresponding source, including base/core and helper source](https://github.com/bsauce42/tape-workshop-mpc-sample/tree/source/v197) is available separately from the autorun download.

Tape Workshop is based on **Melodee by Kerem Kiliç (Ellic Studio)**.

3. Choose Manual Install / update and select **Tape-Workshop-v196-Signed-Update.zip**.
4. When prompted, physically press **B3 / INSTALL** on the MPC and let it restart.
5. Refresh the browser companion after restarting.

Open **Roll → Data Push → MIDI GENERATOR**. Choose a WAV/pad, existing Roll MIDI, or project key; choose Chords, Bass Line, Pluck, Melody or Hybrid; set the target, preview and add to the Roll. releases.name: Beat-Train v1.6
releases.body:
**Pad sounds.** A song can bring its own drum sounds: one hit per pad colour in a `sounds` folder in the song folder (`kick`, `red`, `yellow`, `blue`, `orange`, `green`, as `.wav`, `.ogg` or `.mp3`). [Trackyard](https://github.com/drose030/trackyard) v1.2.0 lets you pick them from the song's drum track. Turn up **PAD SOUNDS** in the settings and every pad plays its drum's sound, so you hear what you play. The song's own drums keep their volume on SHIFT + K2: all the way down to hear only your playing, or a little under it.

**Quicker sound.** A pad sound now comes out about 12 ms after you hit the pad (it was about 46 ms), with no dropouts on the device.

**The highway no longer looks late.** What the screen shows is always a few milliseconds old. The notes are now drawn that far ahead, so they reach the line when you hear them. The timing offset (K1) can stay at 0.

To update, replace `autorun/beattrain` and `autorun/beattrain.sha256` on your card with the ones from `beattrain-mpc-sample.zip`, or copy the whole `autorun` folder. Your songs and settings in `BeatTrain/` stay as they are.

## Download

- **Windows** (64-bit): `Trackyard-Setup-1.3.0.exe`

Install over the old version; your songs, settings and downloaded models stay. The app isn't signed by a registered developer: see the [README](https://github.com/drose030/trackyard#or-the-app-for-mac-or-windows) for the first start.

## New

- **Song overview:** a strip above the footer shows the whole song's waveform, the part in view and where playback is. Click or drag it to move the view.
- **Scroll while playing:** scrolling or zooming during playback no longer jumps back to the playhead. The view follows again once the playhead is back in view, after a jump (ruler, ←/→, Home) or on the next Play.
- **Convert MP3** opens the dialog in the folder of the last converted file.

## Fixed

- Pressing Save again while the folder dialog of a new song was open saved it twice and then broke opening the next file ("Cannot read properties of undefined"). Only one save runs at a time now.

releases.body:
## Download

- **Mac** (Apple Silicon): `Trackyard-1.2.0-arm64.dmg`

## New: pad sounds for Beat-Train

Beat-Train can mute the drum stem and play a real drum sound on each pad strike instead. In the editor, the ♪ button right of each row picks that row's sound from the song's own drum stem:

- It steps through the row's hits (‹ › or ←/→), best first: as few other drums at the same time as possible, ringing out freely, no ghost notes. Each one plays, and the cut is marked in its row.
- **Use this** picks it, **No sound** removes it; undo works as for notes.
- Save writes the picks to `sounds/` in the song folder: `kick.wav`, `red.wav`, `yellow.wav`, `blue.wav`, `orange.wav`, `green.wav`, named after the row colours.

A sound starts 1 ms before the hit's attack in the drum stem, found to the sample, and lasts as long as the hit rings, up to the next hit. With pad sounds on, Beat-Train mutes the whole drum stem, so a pad without a sound stays silent. Songs without a drum stem can't get pad sounds.

releases.name: hdslaveOS 0.9.1-hdslave.1 + MPC Sample plug-ins
releases.body:
> **Back up `Melodee/Projects` before you update.** From 0.9.1 on, the sequencer counts 960 ticks a quarter note, as Melodee 0.9 does. Projects from earlier versions load with their timing kept. A project saved in 0.9.1 plays ten times too slow in hdslaveOS 0.8.3 and earlier.

## Downloads

- **Complete SD-card install** for hdslaveOS and all eleven plug-ins. [Download complete installer](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/releases/download/v0.9.1-hdslave.1/hdslaveOS-MPC-Sample-Complete-SD-Card-Install-v0.9.1-hdslave.1-unsigned.zip)
- **OS-only ZIP** for updating an existing install. [Download OS-only ZIP](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/releases/download/v0.9.1-hdslave.1/hdslaveOS-MPC-Sample-SD-Card-Install-v0.9.1-hdslave.1-unsigned.zip)
- **11-plug-in pack** with the updated hdslave plug-ins. [Download plug-ins](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/releases/download/v0.9.1-hdslave.1/hdslaveOS-MPC-Sample-11-CLAP-Plugins-v0.9.1-hdslave.1.zip)

Back up the card and extract the unsigned ZIP on your computer.
- **First install:** open `START-HERE.txt` in the complete installer.
- **Direct-boot card:** copy both `autorun/` and `autorun.sh` to the card's top level.
- **SampleBoot card:** keep its launcher and copy the contents of `autorun/` into `autorun/mods/hdslaveOS 0.9.1-hdslave.1/`.
- **Plug-ins:** copy the supplied files to `Melodee/Plugins/hdslave/`, and keep their filenames so existing projects can load them.

[Illustrated quickstart](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/blob/v0.9.1-hdslave.1/docs/QUICKSTART.md)

## Changes

**Melodee 0.9.1.** hdslaveOS now tracks Melodee v0.9.1, with its 960-tick sequencer and the rest of upstream's changes. [Upstream Melodee release](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/releases/tag/v0.9.1)

**Stage keys:**
- On a plug-in's **PRESETS** page, **−** and **+** step through its presets ([#1](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/issues/1)).
- Hold **SAMPLE** and press **−** / **+** to move the octave on every Stage page, PANEL and EDIT included. In the Drums layout this moves the bank.
- **−** / **+** and the encoder do nothing on a plug-in shown **STOPPED**.

**A second review of plug-in hosting, with every finding fixed and tested:**
- **Freeze:** an edit asks to unfreeze only for the tracks the plug-in really plays on, the track in hand first.
  - A frozen track's own Stage shows the print and takes no plug-in screen input.
  - A bypassed effect on a frozen chain asks nothing.
  - A parameter, screen or companion edit of a shared plug-in asks for every frozen track that plays it.
- **MIDI Start / Continue:**
  - Start plays from the top, also while playing, and on Song from the song's top.
  - Continue plays from the last Song Position. With none told, it resumes where the song stopped, keeping the place within the bar.
  - A Song Position past a looped song's end folds into the loop.
- **MTC and Song's loop:**
  - A song played from past its loop brace plays to its end.
  - Under MTC or MIDI clock, a looped song keeps going round in phase.
  - The MTC cue lands on the bar it names.
- **Knobs:** K1–K3 right after a track change reach the new track's plug-in. A first turn waits for the screen to name its three knobs, and never lands on a page that has gone.
- **Sleeping plug-ins:**
  - Woken only by a real Play, Stop or jump (no longer on every block at 44.1 kHz or with swing), and also for a Stop and Play inside one block.
  - `steady_time` counts the frames a plug-in slept, was bypassed or frozen, or wasn't run.
  - Song's loop brace is sent as CLAP loop points.
  - A preset or state load runs a sleeping plug-in.
- **Undo, picker and browsers:**
  - Undo keeps a plug-in's settings across several steps and when all 32 entries are in use, and says when old steps are let go.
  - The picker and the Samples browser act on the rows they show.
  - Erase in STARRED or RECENT never offers to delete the file.
  - The Name sheet saves, and names, what it was opened for.

**Plug-ins.** Each version is built from the plug-in's published `main`:

| Plug-in | Was | Now | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anvil | 0.6.7 | 0.6.8 | A place a little off the song's line no longer plays a step twice |
| Slink | 0.8.1 | 0.8.2 | The same for the TB-3PO pattern; its LFOs follow the song under MTC; short notes under a held key sound |
| Necronomicon | 0.2.4 | 0.2.5 | The same for its clocks |
| Mystik | 0.3.5 | 0.3.6 | Hold follows the key or pad that struck last; no gate end is lost or cuts a newer strike; pre-roll steps; late loop wraps; position jitter |
| Nexus | 0.1.8 | 0.1.9 | A synced LFO no longer restarts its cycle on a place a little off the line |
| MoonBass | 0.1.7 | 0.1.8 | A synced LFO's edge no longer repeats, and can't drift under MTC |
| Cortex Filter | 0.3.3 | 0.3.4 | The sequence and the LFO catch up on the time the effect slept |
| Psychic | 0.2.6 | 0.2.6 | Desktop build only |
| Foundry | 0.6.7 | 0.6.7 | Desktop build only |
| Machine | 0.1.7 | 0.1.7 | Desktop build only |
| Reverie | 0.6.4 | 0.6.4 | Unchanged |

`MPC-PLUGINS.tsv` lists the commit and SHA-256 of each CLAP. Slink keeps the filename `hdslave TB-MPC-3-P-0.clap` on the card.

## Checks

- **hdslaveOS:** the ARM64 build passed 110 tests (one skipped, as before), the monkey test and 420 page previews.
- **Audio:** the self-test and three bench hashes are identical to upstream Melodee v0.9.1's own build, bit for bit.
- **Plug-ins:** all eleven passed their build tests and AddressSanitizer, with their sound fingerprints unchanged except one Mystik scenario changed on purpose. All 29 staged CLAPs loaded and played in this build's plug-in host.
- **Tests:** every fix has a test that fails on the build before it.
- **Device:** physical MPC testing is pending for this build. 0.8.3-hdslave.3's − / + preset fix was confirmed on an MPC.

Based on Melodee 0.9.1 by Kerem Kiliç (Ellic Studio).

[Illustrated quickstart](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/blob/v0.8.3-hdslave.3/docs/QUICKSTART.md)

## Changes

**The issue this release fixes, [#1](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/issues/1).** On a plug-in track's **PRESETS** page, **−** and **+** now step through the plug-in's presets, as the encoder does. Before, they moved every pad an octave (in the Drums layout, a bank) with no notice. Plug-ins that map pads to steps or voices then played other steps or went silent.
- At either end of the list, or back on the preset that is playing, nothing loads, so an edited preset stays as it is.
- While the plug-in opens, or if it would not open, − and + do nothing there.
- A frozen track asks to unfreeze first.
- Hold **SAMPLE** and press − or + to move the octave.

**Plug-in hosting.** A review of the whole plug-in path, started from #1, found and fixed these:
- **Undo:** it brings a removed or replaced plug-in back with its settings, also when several steps are undone at once. A plug-in entry that the undo history still names is never reused for another plug-in. If all 32 entries are in use, hdslaveOS says when it lets the oldest undo steps go.
- **The PLUG-INS picker:** it asks before a plug-in replaces a track's sound, acts on the rows it shows while the list is still loading, and lands on the folder you came from.
- **PRESETS:** the list follows the selected track, also after Copy Track. PANEL never loads a preset by mistake right after a track change. A companion screen's program pick asks on a frozen track.
- **Sleep:** sleeping plug-ins wake for one block on Play, Stop and a jump, so they hear the transport. They no longer wake on every block at 44.1 kHz, with swing or at uneven tempos.
- **State:** a crashed bridged plug-in keeps its last good state, and opening another project never carries the last project's plug-in states over.
- **Smaller fixes:** the Samples browser acts on the rows it draws. Erase in STARRED or RECENT never offers to delete the file. The Name sheet saves, and names, what it was opened for. Picking an effect into an empty slot is one undo step.

**Plug-ins.** These versions come from each plug-in's published `main`:

| Plug-in | Was | Now | Fixes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nexus | 0.1.4 | 0.1.7 | 6-op models no longer play another model's leftovers; NOTES keeps its limit with chords on one frame; 6-op notes after a choke keep their attack |
| Mystik | 0.3.3 | 0.3.5 | Hold ends and holds as it should across Play, Stop, the Sequencer switch, auditions and slides |
| Anvil | 0.6.5 | 0.6.7 | No burst after a choke's fade; a hit inside the fade plays whole; a choke over silence leaves the next hit alone |
| Foundry | 0.6.5 | 0.6.7 | GM Key Map no longer plays the Bass Drum on key 0; a re-hit inside a fade eases the old tail out |
| Machine | 0.1.6 | 0.1.7 | The louder of two same-frame hits plays; very short notes sound; same-block chokes stay silent |
| Slink | 0.6.3 | 0.8.1 | The 0.8.0 MPC panel order, a clean filter after long notes, and very short notes in Notes mode |
| Reverie | 0.6.3 | 0.6.4 | A chord let go on its first sample sounds; LP 24 restarts clean |
| Psychic | 0.2.5 | 0.2.6 | Drone sounds after a silence or a drone preset load, also while asleep |
| Necronomicon | 0.2.3 | 0.2.4 | A keyed choke stops the voice |
| Cortex Filter | 0.3.2 | 0.3.3 | The envelope follower stays right while the effect would sleep |
| MoonBass | 0.1.6 | 0.1.7 | A hit sets off a shockwave on the Orbital Impact page; Split Mode is named Key Range |

## Checks

releases.name: MPC Remote addin v1.4.1
releases.body:
**Installer update for MPC OS 3.10.1.** The addin is unchanged from 1.4.0; only the bundled installer is new (open-mpc/mpc-vst-plugins at dbe1f2b).

- Fixes "Read-only file system" under `/etc/systemd/system/acvs.service.d/` when installing or updating on 3.10.1.
- **Gen1 with Akai's user access on (e.g. Key 37):** `/etc` is a read-only overlay stacked on a writable one; the drop-in is written in the writable layer and persists across reboots (open-mpc/mpc-vst-plugins#834).
- **Gen2 (e.g. Live III):** `/etc` is read-only, so the addin loads through a `/run` drop-in. `/run` is cleared at every reboot; the **Addin Restore** patch (Plugin Manager → PATCHES) puts it back at start-up.

Already have Remote? Reinstall it (Plugin Manager or the installer app): an addin installed from an older release keeps its older installer.

---

The MPC screen in a browser, and an MCP server so an AI model can see and touch it, play MIDI and read files.

## Requirements

- A Gen2 MPC OS standalone device (aarch64: Live III, One G2, Key(s) G2). The installer refuses anything else.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Installing addins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r MPC-Remote-addin-1.4.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Remote-addin-1.4.1/install.sh`

The installer copies the addin into `/data/mpc-addins/remote/`, adds `mpc_remote_addin.so` to the `LD_PRELOAD` list of MPC's service
and **restarts MPC** (save your project first). The list is extended, never replaced: other addins and the
libraries the firmware preloads stay. Where no writable file sets the list (the unit is on the read-only root), one
drop-in shared by every addin sets it, `/etc/systemd/system/<service>.service.d/90-mpc-addins.conf`. Re-run the
installer after a firmware update. `-y` skips the question, `-n` leaves the restart to you.

Settings are in `/data/mpc-addins/remote/mpc_remote_addin.conf`; an upgrade keeps your edits.

It listens on the device only. From your computer: ssh -L 6720:127.0.0.1:6720 root@<device address>, then open http://localhost:6720 (bind and port are in mpc_remote_addin.conf).

Uninstalling and the file list are in `INSTALL.md` inside each zip.

---

releases.name: MPC Sample Scale Mode 1.2.0
releases.body:
**MPC Sample Scale Mode 1.2.0.** Hold 16 Levels (about a second) to turn Scale on or off; with Scale on, the 16 Levels slots play a scale, shown on the SCALE page.

Changes since 1.1.0:
- **The page is Scale.** A hold turns Scale and the SCALE page on together, and the next hold turns both off: MPC's screen comes straight back (it used to linger a few seconds, and closing the page with the dial left Scale on). A dial press now exits Scale too. If another page took the screen while Scale is on, a hold brings the SCALE page back.
- **Input lock.** While Scale is on, buttons and knobs no longer reach MPC, so nothing changes MPC's screen or parameters under the page (before, the knobs moved the sample's trim and other settings). The pads, 16 Levels, Shift, the transport (Rec, Overdub, Stop, Play, Play Start), notes 84-87 and the page's own keys, dial and K1-K3 still work. `lock_input=0` turns the lock off; `pass_notes` lists the buttons that get through. Each control kept from MPC is logged with its note.
- `padctl raw [n]` logs the raw control-surface input to MPC's journal.

Checked on an MPC Sample, firmware 1.3.0.12 (2026-11-09): the hold toggle and the input lock, by hand and with injected presses. Notes 84-87 are believed to be the bank buttons; not confirmed yet.

Needs [mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler](https://github.com/jacob-sabella/mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler) **1.0.1** or later for the page. The installer's `LD_PRELOAD` drop-in on the Sample is on `/run`, so reinstall after a reboot (or restore it from the SD card's autorun).

releases.name: MPC Sample Scale Mode 1.1.0
releases.body:
**MPC Sample Scale Mode** (was Enable Scale Mode). **Hold 16 Levels** (about a second) to turn Scale on or off. With Scale on, the 16 Levels slots play a scale instead of their usual steps. A short press is still a normal 16 Levels press, and Shift+16 Levels still cycles the Type.

![The SCALE page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacob-sabella/mpc-addin-sample-scalemode/7f5c90324dbc6f3458eb17466a265d5992d2fade/docs/screenshots/scale-page.png)

Holding 16 Levels also opens a **SCALE page**. It shows the notes every slot plays and lights the one you hit; the soft keys pick scale, root or octave, the dial changes it, K1-K3 set them directly, and a dial press closes it. It stays up while Scale is on.

Needs [mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler](https://github.com/jacob-sabella/mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler) **1.0.1** or later for the page. Without it, the hold still toggles Scale.

**Upgrading from Enable Scale Mode 0.x:** the addin was renamed, so uninstall the old one first: `sh /data/mpc-addins/enable-scalemode/uninstall.sh`. While the old one is loaded, this one stays off and says so in MPC's log. Settings start fresh.

Changes since 1.0.0:
- **Always by ear.** `detect_pitch=always` (or `padctl detect always`) listens to every sample, not only untagged ones, and the note heard wins over the file's tag: for samples tagged with the wrong note. Checked on a Moog lead tagged D that sounds C#: with root A, slot 0 sounded G# by the tag and A by ear. A sample with no clear pitch keeps MPC's root note either way.
- `detect_pitch` takes `untagged` (the default, as in 1.0.0), `always` or `off` (0/1/2 still work); `padctl detect` shows or sets it and saves it to the conf.

Tested on an MPC Sample, firmware 1.3.0.12 (2026-11-06): the device test passes 19 of 19 from this zip, with every slot's pitch and the pad latency measured from the USB audio. The installer's `LD_PRELOAD` drop-in on the Sample is on `/run`, so reinstall after a reboot.

releases.name: RHYTHMER OS 0.2.0 — New sounds. Better flow.
releases.body:
# RHYTHMER OS 0.2.0
## New sounds. Better flow.

More sounds to explore, more direct editing, and a smoother path from your first note to a finished groove.

RHYTHMER OS 0.2.0 brings two new instruments, an updated FMini-1, refined Rhythmer Kit editing, and improvements throughout the track, Acid and Break workflows. Built for exploring Jungle, Techno, House and IDM on your MPC Sample.

### Meet your new instruments

- **Frodhes:** expressive electric pianos, vibraphone and marimba, with 57 original factory programs.
- **Tenebrae:** eight oscillator models spanning basses, leads, pads, keys and more, with 164 programs including Init.
- **FMini-1:** updated to the original 2.6.0 engine, with revised filter response, contour shaping and optimizations, retaining its 200 original factory presets.

### Start a track. Change direction.

TRACK SETUP brings instrument replacement, track types, MPC kit loading and track deletion into one visible menu. Change an instrument or track type while keeping your patterns; delete a track through its separate confirmation.

Press the encoder on an engine-less track to choose its type. On a Sample Kit, pressing it on an empty pad opens sample loading for that pad, including when the whole kit is empty. On-screen hints show the next step.

Change instruments directly from the preset list. Switch tracks while browsing and the screen follows the selected track. Preset browsing wraps from the last sound back to the first, in both directions.

B2 SENDS stays visible in BASIC. Its confirmation can enable FULL and open SENDS directly, or cancel without changing modes. Existing repeat-rate, MOVE/COPY and back controls retain their priority.

### Find a break. Keep the groove.

Browse loops with ORIGINAL or tempo-synchronised SYNC audition before loading them. Replacing a source preserves your existing patterns and performance settings, with clear confirmation when changing the source's bar count.

BREAK GEN and BRK PERF have clearer entry, return and loading controls. Pattern Hold, CHOP, LOOP and STRETCH have more explicit operating hints, while Variation and Stretch feedback show when the performance actions are active.

Loop audition remains separate from the track's musical state, so you can explore another source while keeping your current groove intact.

### Your pad. Your sound.

Rhythmer Kit's EDIT list starts with the selected pad's native **Volume**, followed by its supported Pan, Tune or Decay controls. Related parameters stay together in rows of three, with the whole-kit filter on the next row.

P01–P16 labels identify the pad you are editing; ALL PADS identifies the kit-wide filter. The 36 complete sixteen-pad factory kits retain their mixed-engine flexibility, pad-source replacement and User Kit saving.

Mute individual Rhythmer Kit pads with MUTE + pad, solo a pad with SHIFT + pad in mute mode, and clear project mutes with SHIFT + MUTE. Pad LEDs show the state, which is kept in the project without changing the kit's sound settings. TRACKS retains whole-track mute. Existing release and effect tails decay naturally.

### Shape it. Save it. Come back to it.

Parameter names and ordering are refined across oscillator, filter, envelope, LFO, modulation and effects controls. Source, Destination and Amount stay together, and named choices make settings such as Key Tracking and Polarity easier to read.

Open SAVE SOUND or PAD SOURCE from EDIT, save to one of 64 User Sound or User Kit slots, and reload your sounds from the preset list—even in another project. Save the project separately to keep its patterns and arrangement.

### Save where you choose

First SAVE and SAVE AS let you choose a folder and name. Further SAVE presses update that file. Opening another project or starting NEW offers SAVE, DISCARD or CANCEL instead of automatically overwriting your manual save.

Idle autosave updates one separate recovery entry per project under Rhythmer/Autosave. On the Project home screen, SHIFT + B3 RECOVERY opens the list; load a recovered copy and SAVE it deliberately.

### Build a chord progression

CHORD GEN is a separate instrument-track generator alongside the existing GENERATE Tn / MUTATE Tn workflow. Choose a genre, progression family, 1–8 chord changes and 1–16 bars; adjust rhythmic density, chord complexity, energy, voicing and register, then play the result as Block chords, an arpeggio or a strum.

It follows the project's key and scale by default. Local overrides affect only the generated part. Jazz and neo-soul profiles add extended harmony and voice leading. NEW CHORDS chooses another progression; MUTATE CHORDS keeps the progression while varying articulation. Generation keeps the instrument and other tracks, with Undo/Redo.

Rhythmer Kit retains genre-based drum generation; Acid and Break keep their dedicated generators. The illustrated manual and First Groove guide explain which command to use and how to return from each page.

### Acid, ready to play

Acid GEN keeps its NEW/MUTATE generation behavior while presenting its musical settings across two pages, without exposed seed controls.

Eight original Aphex choices join the Hortator Acid palette: **Acid Squelch, Lead Scream, Whistle Lead, Resonant Spike, Acid Seq, Reso Bass, Filter Cry and Techno Pulse**. Their native sound controls remain available for editing.

### Refinements

A steadier external MIDI BPM display keeps whole-number tempos clean while retaining meaningful fractional readings. The actual sync algorithm is unchanged. Rhythmer Kit animation flows across pad changes, and contextual Note Repeat and ARP controls remain available.

### Fixes

- Preset loading, parameter mapping, pad labels and state restoration.
- Track navigation, Back, confirmation, loading cancellation and Undo/Redo.
- Break playback, performance controls and held-command handling.
- User Sound/User Kit saving and error feedback.

### Make your first groove

The manual and **Your first groove with RHYTHMER OS.** guide cover the current navigation, track types, sound saving, independent Chord GEN and the Break workflow, with visual controls and step-by-step instructions.

[Download & Installation](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/installer/) · [Manual](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/) · [Your first groove](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/quickstart.html)

RHYTHMER OS remains early beta software. Back up your SD card before installing, follow the installation guide, and keep sharing what feels good and what could work better.

Built on Melodee by Kerem Kiliç / Ellic Studio, with thanks to the original engine developers and open-source contributors. Original authorship, licenses and credits are retained.

**RHYTHMER OS — by Jazzy Rhythmer**

*In search of feel-good rhythms.*

## Workflow

- On native Sample Kit SOUND/TRIM, encoder Push opens TRACK TYPE if all 128 pads and layers are empty. SAMPLE KIT starts first-sample loading. If other pads contain samples, Push opens SAMPLES for the selected empty pad. Screen hints show both routes.
- Loaded/layered pads, other editors, recording/Freeze guards, Break loop entry and contextual Note Repeat controls keep their existing jobs. Shift + Push cancels the browser; B1 goes up folders or exits at the root. Sample load Undo preserves other pads.
- Preset lists and main PRESETS browsing wrap in both directions using the encoder or Minus/Plus. Folder lists wrap within the current folder. User Sound/User Kit remain included; absolute pot selection and existing load timing are unchanged.

## Acid Engine

The four original Hortator Acid sounds are retained. Eight unmodified Aphex factory choices are also available: **Acid Squelch, Lead Scream, Whistle Lead, Resonant Spike, Acid Seq, Reso Bass, Filter Cry and Techno Pulse**. They use the original Aphex DSP, native filters and source edit parameters. Source identity and edits persist in projects and User Sound; Rhythmer Kit pad source/restore is also covered.

## Validation

ARM64 build; 19 runtime unit tests; 290 track/input/navigation assertions; GEN/Acid/Break integration; audio self-test; 36,000 random surface moves; 430 UI previews with no text issues. Host regressions cover single instruments, 36 kits, engine/kit filters and 4,587 control round trips. All eight aliases match original Aphex control values and pass five-note output, project/User Sound and pad-source restore checks under ASan/UBSan for the host code. Original native DSP libraries are unchanged and not all are sanitizer-instrumented. Signed-update identity and tamper checks pass.

This is early beta software.  No break recordings are bundled.

[Download & installation](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/installer/) · [Manual](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/) · [Your first groove](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/quickstart.html)

Based on Melodee by Kerem Kiliç (Ellic Studio) and the credited open-source engine projects. SOURCE, MOVE-SOURCE and SUPPORT-SOURCE provide corresponding source and notices.

releases.name: MPCTRACKER 0.1.0
releases.body:
First release of MPCTRACKER, a pattern tracker for the Akai MPC Sample that runs from an SD card.

It has eight tracks and 64 sample slots, and it uses the ProTracker effect column. It loads WAV files and 4 to 8 channel .mod files, saves songs to the card, and starts with a short VHS style intro that any pad skips. The README has the full list of controls.

## Installing

1. Read the Safety section of the README, save the project that is open on the sampler and back up the card.
2. Unzip `mpctracker-v0.1.0-sd-card.zip` and copy the `autorun` and `tracker` folders to the root of the SD card. This replaces any `autorun` folder that is already on the card.
3. Put WAV files in `tracker/samples`, or browse to samples that are already on the card.
4. Insert the card. The tracker starts a few seconds after the sampler has booted.
5. Hold SHIFT and press STOP to quit back to the sampler. Take the card out and power cycle for a normal boot.

## Notes

This was developed against the emulator on firmware 1.3.0.12. It starts and plays sound on a real unit, but most of the hardware testing is still to do, so expect rough edges. It never touches the sampler's internal storage and it only writes inside the `tracker` folder on the card.

The zip has no demo song. A first run plays a built-in drum kit and groove. Copy a `.mod` file into `tracker/songs` before the first start and it opens that instead.

Still to come are sampling from the inputs, block copy and paste, a fill tool, naming songs on the device, a view of all eight tracks at once, and MIDI.

## Fixed

- **Step Edit's SLICE card.** On a kit step's **SOUND** cards, **K2** (**SLICE**) shows **PAD**, the slice (**5 / 16**) or **RND**. The panel shows the slices of the step's sample with the step's slice lit, and **B2** (**SLICES**) on the sounds shows them numbered. In 0.9.0, **K2** set the slice but its card, the slice edges and **SLICES** stayed blank.

Everything new in 0.9.0 is in its [release notes](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/releases/tag/v0.9.0) and in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

releases.name: Melodee 0.9.0
releases.body:
Melodee 0.9.0 for the Akai MPC Sample: a 16-track groovebox that runs on the MPC in place of the stock app, from the microSD card.

This page lists the changes in 0.9.0, then those in 0.8.0 to 0.8.3.

# 0.9.0

## Update

- **From 0.2.x to 0.8.3:** copy `Melodee-MPC-Sample-v0.9.0.zip` to the card, or send it from the web page at http://melodee.local. Melodee asks *Update to v0.9.0?*, saves, installs and restarts. On firmware 1.4.0.7 this works from 0.6.6.
- **Firmware 1.4.0.8:** 0.7.1 and earlier do not start on it. Update Melodee first, then the firmware. Already on 1.4.0.8: install by hand as in [Install](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample#install): turn on **Developer Mode**, unzip, and copy the `autorun` folder and the `autorun.sh` file to the top level of the card. Moving from 1.3.0.12 to 1.4, copy the zip's `autorun.sh` to the top level of the card too.
- **On firmware 1.4.0.7 from 0.6.5 or earlier, from 0.1.0, or a new card:** install by hand as in [Install](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample#install).
- **With SampleBoot:** replace Melodee's folder in `autorun/mods/` with the zip's `autorun` folder.

Requires an MPC Sample on firmware **1.3.0.12**, **1.4.0.7** or **1.4.0.8**.

Back up `Melodee/Projects` before you update. Projects from earlier versions open as they were. A project saved in 0.9.0 plays ten times too slow in 0.8.3 and earlier.

## Changed: read this first

- **960 ticks a quarter.** The sequencer counts 960 ticks a quarter note, as the MPC does (96 before). MPC projects import without rounding. Projects from earlier versions load with their timing kept.
- **A fader target you pick stays** (#57). On the Fader page, the target you choose with the encoder is pinned: a plug-in's **FILTER**, **ECHO** and **SPACE** and the knobs of other pages no longer take the fader. **B2** unpins it. **K1**–**K3** on the Fader page still take it.
- **Chop's pads play through the kit pad.** When a kit pad holds the sample, a slice's pad plays the slice through that kit pad, with its tune, envelopes, filter, Warp, Mono/Poly and Pad FX, as its recorded hits do. Taps overlap.

## New

### Sequencer

- **Track speed** (#67): ×1/64, ×1/32, ×1/16, ×1/8, ×¼, ×½, ×¾, ×1, ×1½, ×2 or ×4. On Patterns, **SHIFT** + **K3** (**SPEED**). At ×1/64 one bar of the pattern lasts 64 bars. See [Track speed](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/tracks.md#track-speed).
- **Track direction** (#67): on Patterns, **SHIFT** + **LOOP** sets **FWD**, **REV** or **RND**. **REV** plays the last step first. **RND** plays every step once a pass, in a new order each pass; the orders are the same each time the pattern plays from the top. The track list shows ▶, ◀ or a die. See [Track direction](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/tracks.md#track-direction).
- **A step's own sound** (#67): on a kit or keygroup track, **B1** on Step Edit has a fourth card set, **SOUND**.
  - **K1** (**SOUND**): any sample on a kit or keygroup pad of the project. The step plays it through its own pad.
  - **K2** (**SLICE**): a slice of the sample's chop, or **RND**.
  - **K3** (**PLAY**): **FWD**, **REV** or **RND**.
  - Hold a step and press **SAMPLE SELECT** to pick the sound on the pads. **ERASE** + knob sets a card back to **PAD**.
  - See [The pattern editors](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/sequencing.md#the-pattern-editors).
- **Pattern lengths** (#52): **K1** on Patterns sets 1 to 16 bars one bar at a time, then 24, 32, 48, 64, 96 and 128 bars.
- **Up to 128 bars:** Looper lengths 32, 64 and 128 bars; Sample Record's length 24 to 128 bars; a song clip 1 to 128 bars. A loop longer than 64 s gets memory made for it: the first press says *making memory, press again*.

### Samples

- **Trim before loading.** In the sample browser, turn **K2** (**START**) or **K3** (**END**) to open the trim view: the whole sample and a closer view. The encoder moves the point in finer steps. Push loads the sample onto the last pad you hit with that start and end; **SHIFT** + pad loads it onto the next empty pad. **ERASE** sets both back. The file on the card is not changed. See [Trim a sample before loading it](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/kits-and-sampling.md#trim-a-sample-before-loading-it).
- **Reverse one slice.** On Chop, **SHIFT** + **LOOP** reverses the slice in hand. A reversed slice shows an arrow. **TO PADS** and the **MPC 3** export lay it as a reversed pad. One undo.

### File sharing

- While Melodee runs, a computer connected with USB-C can open the card as a network drive. Melodee keeps working and keeps the card.
- On a Mac, choose **Melodee** under **Network** in the Finder sidebar, or **Go** > **Connect to Server** and **smb://melodee.local**. On Windows, open `\\192.168.155.1`. Connect as **Guest** and open **SD Card**.
- On until you turn it off in **SETTINGS** > **AUDIO** > **File sharing**. Needs firmware 1.3.0.12; on firmware 1.4 it does not start.
- See [File sharing](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/projects-and-files.md#file-sharing).

### Projects

- **SAVE AS with Autosave off** (#63): **SHIFT** + **B1** on the Project page.
- **Undo** keeps the last 512 steps (32 before), up to 64 MB.

## Fixed

- **Decay From Start** (#64): a one shot fades to silence over its decay, whatever its sustain. Sustain is for Note On mode. The Stage picture shows it.
- **Copy a pad to another kit** (#48): **SHIFT** + **ERASE**, the source pad, then hold **PAD BANK** and press the other kit's track pad, then the target pad. The copy came from the new track's own pad before.
- **SAMPLE SELECT on an audio track** (#53) no longer crashes Melodee when sounds of your own are saved.
- **Pad colours** (#69): the sixteen colours light the pads as vivid as the screen draws them. On Stage **COLOUR**, **Kit** (the colour the MPC kit brought) comes back at the end of the list after another colour is picked.

## Faster

- Saving a project goes through the sample slots in use only.
- Kit pads played into submixes take less work on every block.

# 0.8.0 to 0.8.3

## Changed: read this first

- **The mixer replaces Tracks and Sends** (0.8.0). **PAD FX** + **KNOB FX** opens it. Stage's **MIX** and **SENDS** are gone: a track's level, pan and sends are on the mixer, and **B3** on Stage is **FX**. On a kit, **B3** still has **SENDS** for the pads' own sends.
- **The mixer opens on the strips** (0.8.2): every channel of the row side by side. Hold **+** for the selected channel's card, hold **−** to go back. **−** / **+** act when you let go.
- **Track speed** is on Patterns, **SHIFT** + **K3** (0.8.0). The metronome level is on Tempo.
- **CPU** shows in the Menu's header (0.8.0).
- **Plug-in tracks have no separate Edit page** (0.8.0). Picking a plug-in opens Stage on **EDIT**; **PANEL** is the plug-in's own screen. Hold **SHIFT** on a **B1** page: **B1** (**PLUG-INS**), **B2** (**PRESETS**), **B3** (**TRANSPORT**).
- **Sequences keep track mutes** (0.8.3). Launching a sequence sets its mutes at the next bar (at once when stopped).

## New

- **Mixer** (0.8.0). Every track plays through its effect chain, then its strip: trim, nine-band EQ, compressor, width; then level and pan. **B1** (**SENDS**, then **FX**), **B2** (**EQ**), **B3** (**COMP**). See [The mixer](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/mixer-and-effects.md#the-mixer).
  - **PAD BANK** shows the second row: eight submixes, buses A–D, the input and the master.
  - In mute mode, a pad mutes its channel and **SHIFT** + pad solos it.
  - With **SEQ RECORD** on, level, pan, sends and strip are recorded as Motion lanes.
- **Pad outputs** (0.8.0): a kit pad plays into the kit or into submix 1–8. Kit's Stage **SENDS**, **SHIFT** + **K2** (**OUTPUT**).
- **USB out** (0.8.0): **SETTINGS** > **AUDIO** > **USB out** sends **Tracks** (1–16, mono) or **Submixes** (1–8, stereo) to inputs 3–18.
- **Pad stems** (0.8.0): **STEMS** writes each kit pad the song plays as a WAV of its own, in a folder for each kit, and one WAV for each submix. When one play of the song cannot write them all, it plays again (*Stems: pass 2 of 3*).
- **MPC 3 export** sends each track to the same submix in MPC 3 (0.8.0). **MPC 3** and **LIVE SET** say *mixer settings left out* when the project has settings they cannot carry.
- **Companion screens** (0.8.0): a VST2 plug-in gets a page of its own from a screen folder in `Melodee/Plugin Screens/`. See [Companion screens](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/PLUGIN_COMPANIONS.md).
- **CLAP presets in folders** (0.8.0): a preset location with `/` in its name lists as folders on **PRESETS**.
- **The browsers start at the top of the card** the first time, then where you left them (0.8.0).
- **Firmware 1.4.0.8** (0.8.0).
- **Copy a sequence** (0.8.3): on Sequences, **SHIFT** + **ERASE**, the sequence, then where it goes. Its patterns are copied too.
- **Clear one lock** (0.8.3): hold a step, hold **ERASE** and turn the lock's knob.
- **Plug-in pages** take **MUTE** and **ERASE** taps (0.8.3).

## Fixed

- **MIDI tracks after Play** (#59, 0.8.3): notes play from the first bar after Play, Locate or MTC.
- **Plug-ins at exit** (0.8.3): a CLAP or VST2 plug-in built with a static C++ runtime no longer crashes Melodee when it is unloaded.
- **Echo and reverb tails** (0.8.1): an effect plug-in keeps running for the tail it reports, up to 10 seconds.
- **Presets on a plug-in at rest** (0.8.1): a preset picked for a sleeping CLAP plug-in takes effect at once.
- **A sustain pedal left down** (0.8.1) no longer keeps a plug-in instrument running: All Sound Off (CC 120) and Reset All Controllers (CC 121) lift it.

## Faster

- The screen copies the kits and the pattern overviews only after a change (0.8.1).
- Plug-ins take less work on every block (0.8.1).
- 32-bit VST2 plug-ins: Melodee sleeps until a slow plug-in answers instead of keeping a core busy (0.8.1).
- The controls' lights no longer go through all 8,192 sample slots every 5 ms (0.8.1).

releases.name: Melodee Chip 1.0.0
releases.body:
Melodee Chip 1.0.0 is a chip voice synth with ring mod and sync, a pulse width LFO, crush, a multimode filter, a mod matrix and factory sounds. It is an [Open MPC](https://open-mpc.github.io) plug-in for [Melodee](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample) on the Akai MPC Sample and for MPC OS standalone devices.

## Melodee on the MPC Sample

1. Download `Melodee-Chip-1.0.0-mpc-sample.zip` below.
2. Unzip it. It holds one folder, `Ellic Studio - VST - Melodee Chip`.
3. Copy that folder into the `Plugins` folder at the top level of the SD card. Make the `Plugins` folder if the card has none.
4. In Melodee, select an empty track, press **SAMPLE**, then **B1** (**SYNTH**), and load Melodee Chip.

A project saved with Melodee's built-in SID engine (Melodee 0.1.0-alpha.6 and earlier) opens with that track on Melodee Chip, as it sounded.

## MPC OS devices

- `Melodee-Chip-1.0.0-mpc-aarch64.zip`: Gen2 devices (64-bit ARM) on MPC OS 3.x.
- `Melodee-Chip-1.0.0-mpc-armv7.zip`: Gen1 devices (MPC Live, Live II, One, X, Key 61, Force) on MPC OS 3.x.

Installing needs root shell access (SSH) to the device, so it is for modded units only. Each zip has an `install.sh` and an `INSTALL.md` with the scripted and manual steps. Back up first; use at your own risk.

## Status

The armv7 and aarch64 builds pass the synth's own checks and the Open MPC toolchain's port test. The aarch64 build is tested in Melodee on the MPC Sample. It has not been tested on an MPC OS device yet.

releases.name: USB DeClick v0.1.0 Beta 1
releases.body:
# USB DeClick v0.1.0-beta.1 — First Public Beta

**Experimental USB click-reduction patch for Akai MPC Sample, tested with Google Pixel 8a (Android 16).**

USB DeClick reduces recurring, sharp digital clicks that can occur when sampling a phone's audio over USB. It runs on the MPC from an SD card, without an Android companion app or permanent firmware modification.

## What this beta includes

- **Real-time PCM click repair** that tracks a recurring 10 ms spike pattern and corrects strong, isolated stereo impulses using neighboring audio frames.
- **Manual ON/OFF control.** Edit `autorun/USB_DECLICK_MODE.txt` before startup. `ON` enables repair. With `OFF`, the MPC application starts without modification.
- **Targeted USB capture processing** for the MPC's 44.1 kHz, stereo, 32-bit USB audio input.
- **Fixed-size audio state** with no filesystem writes from the PCM processing loop. Long-term CPU and RAM usage on the MPC still need measurement.
- **Removable SD-card installation** with rollback by restarting the MPC without the mod card.
- **Monochrome startup screen** showing that the mod was launched.

## Test evidence

The issue was investigated on a **Google Pixel 8a (Android 16)** connected to an **Akai MPC Sample (firmware 1.3.0.12)**. Recordings showed isolated stereo sample spikes following a **441-frame / 10 ms pattern** at 44.1 kHz.

In a controlled comparison of approximately one-minute recordings of the same track at similar volume, the detector found the following counts.

| Without repair | With repair |
| ---: | ---: |
| 1,335 strong-spike candidates | 25 strong-spike candidates |

The detector found **approximately 98.1% fewer strong-spike candidates** in this comparison. The test used a development build with the same audio repair core as this beta. The beta produced qualitatively similar results on the MPC. A separate controlled benchmark for this beta is still pending.

Some audible artifacts may remain, and results may vary across devices. See the [research findings](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/docs/research-findings.md) and [reproducible test methodology](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/docs/testing-method.md).

## Device support

**The Pixel 8a is the only affected phone tested so far.** A Samsung Galaxy A06 and a laptop produced clean control recordings on the same MPC. Compatibility with other affected phones remains unverified. Reports from other devices are welcome.

## Installation and safety

Download the **SD install ZIP** attached to this release and follow the [installation guide](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/INSTALL.md).

The repair is experimental. Some clicks may remain, and `ON` may alter genuine sharp musical transients. Use `OFF` when repair is unnecessary. To switch modes, edit the mode file and reboot. There is no on-screen toggle. Keep this installation separate from other autorun modifications.

**To roll back**, power off the MPC, remove the mod SD card, and reboot. Installation leaves the internal firmware intact.

## Help improve it

Share your phone and MPC models, firmware, test conditions, `ON` or `OFF` setting, and, if possible, two recordings of the same passage. Use the [community test report template](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/docs/community-test-report.md).

**Unofficial experimental beta. No affiliation with or endorsement by Akai.**
